items.title: HOMEMADE SPECIALTY MALTS 🍺 This Time We Got It RIGHT!
items.description: Today we're making our homemade specialty malts again, this time following the valuable advice many of you left in the comments on the previous video. 🍺 📚 The recipe and further information on homemade specialty malts are available in our book dedicated to homebrewing. Of course, you can find the correct recipe here in the book 👍: https://amzn.to/4sZDU24 The first experiment had several errors, and as you know, I have no problem showing you when something doesn't go as it should. In fact, I think mistakes are an important part of homebrewing: you try, you make mistakes, you study, and you try again! In this video, we start with Pilsner malt and create several specialty malts at home: 🍺 Biscuit/Amber Malt 🍺 Caramel Malt 🍺 Crystal Malt 🍺 Chocolate Malt 🍺 Black Malt We start with 1 kg of Pilsner malt and hydrate it with room-temperature water. We then mash it at about 70°C for 90 minutes, allowing the enzymes in the malt to convert the starches into sugars. We then divide the malt and proceed with different roastings to achieve different colors and characteristics. ⚠️ During roasting, it's important to check and stir the malts frequently. Chocolate and Black malts in particular must be stirred very often to prevent the top part from burning while the bottom part remains less roasted. 🔥 And watch out for smoke! A lot of it can be produced when roasting specialty malts, so it's essential to work in a well-ventilated environment and pay attention to the temperature. 🍺 AN IMPORTANT TIP The malt used for this experiment was already milled. If you want a more precise result, it's best to start with whole malt and proceed with the milling later. For the mash, we experimented with different amounts of water. As a guide, for 1 kg of malt, you can use about 1 liter of water, while a larger amount can facilitate the conversion of starches during the mash. The final result will also depend on your oven and how well you control temperature and humidity. 🍺 HOMEMADE SPECIALTY MALTS: IS IT WORTH IT? This experiment was born out of a desire to see if it's possible to homemade some of the specialty malts typically purchased from breweries and homebrewers. The final result was much more satisfying than the first attempt, and this time we also followed many of the suggestions from our community. 💬 Have you ever tried toasting or caramelizing malt at home? If you followed this recipe or have any tips to add, please leave them in the comments. items.title: My “WRONG STOUT” 🍺 I Broke All the Rules…😱
items.description: Today we're brewing a beer we've decided to call WRONG STOUT, a completely unconventional Stout! 🍺 Recipe found in our book 😉 The EASY WAY to BREW BEER📕 Book : https://amzn.to/3T3ZLZl 🍺 Why "wrong"? Because in this recipe, we do practically everything differently than a traditional Stout: we use specialty house-roasted malts, rolled oats and flaked barley, wild hops, and fermentation at a temperature significantly higher than ideal. The result? A dark, intensely colored beer with a relatively low alcohol content, good body, a light sweetness, and a significant hint of bitterness. During the tasting, we realized that perhaps the most fitting name would be Stout IPA! 😄 🍺 INGREDIENTS Malts and Grains: 2 kg Pilsner Malt 110 g Amber Malt 80 g Caramel Malt 150 g Crystal Malt 110 g Chocolate Malt 90 g Black Malt 65 g Oat Flakes 70 g Barley Flakes Hops: 20 g Wild Hops 10 g Styrian Goldings 10 g Apollo Hops for Dry Hopping, according to the recipe Other Ingredients: 13 liters of water for mashing 3 liters of water for washing the grains Juice of 1 lemon to adjust the pH Brewer's Yeast Sugar for bottle fermentation The home-roasted malts contributed to a higher final gravity and therefore a beer with more body, less alcohol, and a slight sweetness, while the hops provided A significant bitter component. For the tasting, we invited Naodi, who tastes beer without knowing exactly what to expect. The result surprised us: the beer is truly good! The color is intense, the head is persistent, and the flavor is completely different from that of a traditional Stout. A beer born from a series of experiments and "mistakes" that ultimately turned out to be... items.title: PRICKLY PEAR JAM 🌵🍯 How to Pick & Clean IT Without Getting Pricked!
items.description: Today we're making homemade prickly pear jam 🌵🍯, starting with freshly picked prickly pears! I'll show you how to safely harvest prickly pears, including a simple trick using a plastic bottle as a homemade picking tool. 🌵 Ingredients: Prickly pears 1 kg 50 g (1.8 oz) sugar Juice of 1 lemon After cooking, we pour the hot jam into small jars and finally find out how much jam we actually get from more than 2 kg of prickly pears! For the tasting, I paired the jam with homemade sausage meatballs… and the combination was absolutely amazing! 😋 Of course, you can also enjoy this homemade prickly pear jam the simple way — spread on a slice of toasted bread. I also talk about making prickly pear wine. If you'd like to try that, you'll find the recipe here on the channel! ⚠️ IMPORTANT: Prickly pears have extremely fine, irritating spines. items.title: HOMEMADE FIG JAM 🍯 The Secret Ingredient? FIG LEAVES! 🍃
items.description: Today we're making a homemade fig jam, but with a special ingredient: fig leaves! 🍃 This time, we won't use traditional lemon zest to flavor the figs. The goal is to capture that typical summery scent of figs you get when you pass by a fig tree in the summer. And I think the result is truly spectacular! 🍯 INGREDIENTS: 1.5 kg fresh figs 300 g sugar 5 fig leaves Juice of ½ lemon or ½ glass water or wine Once ready, the jam is transferred while still hot into jars and left to cool. 🍃 WHY USE FIG LEAVES? Fig leaves, especially during the summer, release a very distinctive scent. In this recipe, we use them to impart that flavor to the jam, without leaving the leaves inside the jars. The result is a fragrant, sweet fig jam, perfect for breakfast, spread on bread, or paired with a good cheese. 💬 Have you ever used fig leaves in the kitchen? If you try this recipe, let me know in the comments how it turned out! items.title: Homemade Mint Liqueur 🌿 Easy Recipe
items.description: Today we're making a delicious homemade mint liqueur! This refreshing liqueur is incredibly easy to prepare using fresh mint leaves, pure alcohol, sugar, water, and a small piece of lemon peel. After just three days of infusion, we'll prepare a simple syrup, combine everything together, and let the liqueur mature for a couple of weeks. The result is a smooth, refreshing mint liqueur with an alcohol content of approximately 42% ABV, perfect served ice cold after dinner or on a hot summer day. This recipe is not included in our first Homemade Liqueurs book because we're saving it for a possible Volume 2. If you'd like to see a second book with even more homemade liqueur recipes, let us know in the comments! Ingredients About 100 fresh mint leaves 250 ml (8.5 fl oz) 96% neutral alcohol (food-grade ethanol) 250 ml (8.5 fl oz) water 100 g (½ cup) sugar A small piece of lemon peel Directions • Infuse the mint leaves and lemon peel in the alcohol for 3 days. • Shake the jar whenever you walk past it. • Prepare a simple syrup using the water and sugar. • Filter the alcohol infusion and mix it with the cooled syrup. • Let the liqueur mature for at least two weeks before tasting. If you make homemade liqueurs and want to calculate the alcohol percentage of your own recipes, visit our website where we've created a free alcohol calculator.
